subject: Archaeology
title: Eridu: The First City
description: A quick, practical guide to Eridu: The First City.

hook.text: Sumerian myths said the gods chose Eridu as the first city on earth. Archaeology suggests they may have been right.

buildup.text: Eridu dates to around 5400 BCE in southern Iraq. It began as a tiny shrine and grew into a temple complex over 4,000 years.

discovery.text: Excavations revealed 18 temple layers stacked on top of each other — the oldest was a simple reed hut with an altar.

twist.text: Fish bones surrounded every temple level. The god Enki was lord of fresh water and fish — offerings stayed consistent.

climax.text: Eridu shows how a sacred site grew into a city. Religion, not trade or war, may have sparked urban civilization.

punchline.text: The oldest city on earth began as a tiny shrine. Faith built civilization.

quiz.question: What do the 18 temple layers at Eridu suggest?
options: The city was destroyed and rebuilt 18 times by invaders
Continuous worship at the same site for thousands of years — religion may have sparked urbanization
Each layer represents a different civilization that occupied the site

details.summary: Eridu, in southern Iraq, is considered the world's oldest city, dating to around 5400 BCE. Excavations revealed a sequence of temples built one atop another over millennia, showing how a small shrine grew into a monumental religious center at the heart of Sumerian culture.
details.whyItMatters: Eridu shows the transition from village to city. Its temple layers reveal how religious architecture and social complexity grew hand in hand, providing a model for urban origins worldwide.
takeaways: Eridu dates to around 5400 BCE in southern Iraq
Eighteen temple layers show continuous religious building
It models the transition from village to urban center

faq.question: Why do archaeologists call Eridu the first city?
faq.answer: Eridu has the oldest continuous temple sequence known, spanning thousands of years. Sumerian tradition also named it the first city where kingship descended from heaven. Its archaeological record and cultural significance both point to urban origins.

faq.question: What did archaeologists find at Eridu?
faq.answer: Eighteen superimposed temples, the earliest a simple one-room shrine. They also found evidence of fish offerings, pottery, and a surrounding settlement that grew as the temple complex expanded over millennia.
